newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwandans evacuate town as Zaire war spills over.
newsitem.headline: Rwandans evacuate town as Zaire war spills over.

text.p: Thousands fled from the Rwandan town of Gisenyi on Friday as Rwandan and Zairean forces exchanged fire across the border.
In the Rwandan capital of Kigali, Rwandan officials accused Zairean forces of starting the exchanges by hitting Gisenyi town, a refugee camp and near a Rwandan army position.
The town began emptying after three mortar bombs fired from Zaire hit Gisenyi and the Rwanda Patriotic Army (RPA) fired back into Zaire.
At least two people -- a man and a woman -- were wounded in the mortar exchanges and taken to Gisenyi hosptial.
The evacuation of Gisenyi was the worst instance of two weeks of fighting pitting Zairean troops against Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire affecting life on the Rwandan side of the border.
I spent three hours pinned down under fire in Gisenyi on Friday morning.
Zairean and Rwandan troops fired back and forth across the border and it seemed to be targeted and not just stray fire.
Heavy firing across the border continued into the afternoon. The Rwandan army fired back with artillery, mortars and automatic weapons from the hills surrounding Gisenyi.
The town's residents appeared very frightened and were trekking out of the lakeside town or emptying their houses.
In the Rwandan capital of Kigali, Emmanuel Ndahiro, special adviser to Rwandan military strongman Paul Kagame, said the Zaireans opened fire from Mogoma, the highest point in Goma city.

"They are using 37 mm anti-aircraft guns hidden in four different places. Six or seven shells hit the market in Gisenyi, a refugee camp, close to an RPA position and close to a court building," he told Reuters.
"My only interpretation is that this is a provocation," he said.

Zaire accuses Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of fighting in eastern Zaire and state radio said on Friday its transitional parliament had voted to sever diplomatic relations with its three eastern neighbours.
